name: Snd
editorial_article: "Snd" is the 1996 debut studio album by the experimental electronic project Microstoria, a collaboration between German musicians Jan St. Werner (known for his work with Mouse on Mars) and Markus Popp (the architect of Oval). Released via the influential electronic label Mille Plateaux—and concurrently on Thrill Jockey in the US—the album stands as a seminal document of the mid-90s "clicks and cuts" movement, a micro-genre characterized by the aestheticization of digital artifacts, glitch, and sonic detritus. \n\nMusically, "Snd" avoids traditional melodic or rhythmic structures, instead opting for a landscape of pulsating fragments, quavering, polyphonous bubbles, and warm synth textures. Its departure from conventional beat-driven electronica allowed it to serve as a bridge between the ambient textures of early 90s IDM and the rigorous, deconstructive approach that would later define the glitch movement. The record’s conceptual weight is mirrored in its cold, precise production, which treats digital glitches not as errors but as intentional, malleable building blocks. The album’s enduring influence is underscored by its subsequent remix companion, "Reprovisers," which invited other electronic artists to further deconstruct its material. For listeners navigating the evolution of experimental sound design, "Snd" remains a pivotal exploration of the beauty inherent in digital imperfection.
